items.body:
## Summary
`pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` `fold_authorisation` (landed today via PR #3888, closing #3800) selects the live version with `max_by_key(|(_, body)| body.version)` (currency.rs:313-320). When two distinct signed bodies from the expected issuer carry the **same highest version** (a forked/duplicated issuer chain, or a re-issued v2 with a different rate), `Iterator::max_by_key` returns the **last** maximal element in slice order — so the folded `Live` authorisation depends on the order the caller happens to present the objects, not on the objects alone. The module header promises "State is a fold over the objects alone" (currency.rs:20-23), and the revoke side of the same fold was made explicitly deterministic ("ties break to the smallest `revoked_version_from`, deterministically", currency.rs:296-300) — the version selection has no such tie-break.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe)
Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-currency/` on the laptop — verbatim `validate` + version-selection core of `fold_authorisation`, against `currency.rs` at main `c3fda1c4` (sha256 `8f68982526219dff920586495a076d2c1a33f87fe3b6716a74e561ea821b9493`, reference copy in the probe dir).

Two issuer-signed v2 bodies for authorisation 7, `rate_num` 8000 vs 9000:

```
order [8000,9000] -> rate_num 9000
order [9000,8000] -> rate_num 8000
test duplicate_version_fold_depends_on_input_order ... ok
```

Same object set, two presentation orders, two different live rates.

## Why it matters
The fold is the library source of truth every later phase consumes: Phase 2 (#3801) folds "highest version" at submission time and Phase 3 (#3802) binds quotes to it. Two nodes (or one node after a re-sync that changes object order) can fold the same signed object set to different live rates and both be "correct" per this code — a consensus-style divergence in a money-adjacent type, created by the issuer merely signing two bodies at one version (which the chain permits on forked chains; nothing in `validate` or the fold rejects duplicate versions).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Duplicate highest versions fold deterministically regardless of input order: either a canonical tie-break (e.g. by body hash / canonical bytes) documented in the fold's doc comment, or duplicate versions at the maximum are rejected / fold to no live authorisation with the rule stated.
- [ ] Regression test: the same duplicate-version object set in both orders folds to the identical state.
- [ ] Existing currency tests (golden rates, hijack, revoke tie-break) still pass.
- [ ] The chosen rule is recorded on #2290 (parent design) if it changes the design record's fold semantics.

Distinct from: #3801 (gateway live-state checks — it consumes this fold), #3802 (quote binding), #4060/#4063 (app_manifest validation, different module).

items.body:
# id(currency): `sign_authorisation` never calls `validate` — a signed authorisation naming another issuer or with `rate_den = 0` is dead on arrival, and signing succeeds silently

## Summary

`pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` has exactly one validity contract for a `RateAuthorisation` body — `RateAuthorisation::validate` (issuer must equal the event author; `rate_den` must be non-zero) — and the fold enforces it (`fold_authorisation` filters on `body.validate(author).is_ok()`, currency.rs:299 at origin/main `a2b4345e80`). But the signing entry point, `sign_authorisation` (currency.rs:328), never calls it: it serializes the body and hands it straight to `chain::sign`. A signer can therefore produce a properly signed, chain-valid event whose body is invalid by the module's own two hard rules, and nothing anywhere will ever fold it as `Live`:

- **Issuer mismatch:** body names issuer B, signed by A. `fold_authorisation(.., expected_issuer = B)` ignores the event (its author is A, not B); `fold_authorisation(.., expected_issuer = A)` drops the body at the `validate` filter (body names B). The signed object is unreachable in every fold.
- **`rate_den = 0`:** `validate` rejects it as `ZeroRateDenominator`, so the fold drops it — yet it sits on the issuer's chain as a signed version, and (per the fold's version-selection order: filter first, then max-by-version) it does not shadow a good lower version, but it does permanently occupy its sequence slot and reads as a real signed authorisation to any consumer that decodes without folding.

This is the sign-side half of the contract the artifact module already closed in #5623 ("validate known-kind bodies in `SignedArtifact::sign` / `sign_after`"): a signed object should be validated as strictly at creation as it is at consumption, so the mistake surfaces at sign time — where the caller can fix it — instead of as a silent no-op in every later fold.

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main `a2b4345e80`)

- `git grep -n "validate" pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` returns exactly three sites: the definition (currency.rs:153), the fold filter (currency.rs:299), and one test (currency.rs:513). `sign_authorisation` and `sign_revoke` contain no validation call.
- Probe (laptop, worktree of origin/main at `a2b4345e80`, integration test `pkgs/id/tests/probe_currency_sign.rs` in worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-currency-sign-wt`, run with `cargo test --test probe_currency_sign -- --nocapture`): `sign(issuer-mismatch body) -> Ok`, `sign(rate_den=0 body) -> Ok`, `sign(valid body) -> Ok` (control), and the mismatched body folds to `None` for both the signing issuer and the named issuer — dead on arrival, exactly as the code reading predicts. (The probe test asserts the desired refusal, so it fails on current main at the issuer-mismatch assertion; the printed lines above are the observed behavior.)
- Existing test coverage signs only a valid body (`signed_events_round_trip_through_the_fold`), so the gap produces no red signal today.

## Why it matters

`sign_authorisation` is the only sanctioned way to create these objects (Phase 1 of #2290; the conversion engine #5536 builds on it). An LP tool that mis-sets `issuer_id` (e.g. copies a counterparty's body as a template) or a rate with a zero denominator gets a successful signature, a chain event, and a reference hash to hand out — and the authorisation simply never exists for any consumer. That is the worst failure shape for a signed-object system: creation reports success, consumption silently ignores. Failing at sign time with the existing `ValidateError` vocabulary costs one call; the artifact precedent (#5623) shows the fleet's chosen shape for exactly this fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sign_authorisation` refuses a body that `validate` would reject for the signing key's issuer (issuer mismatch, `rate_den = 0`), surfacing the refusal through `SignError` (a new variant wrapping `ValidateError` is fine); no event is produced for an invalid body.
- [ ] Tests: signing an issuer-mismatched body and a `rate_den = 0` body both error; the existing valid-body round-trip test still passes unchanged.
- [ ] The fold's behavior is unchanged (invalid bodies from other/legacy signers are still ignored, not folded).
- [ ] Out of scope: extending `validate`'s rule set — that is #4071, open separately. This issue only enforces the two rules that already exist, at sign time.

## Notes

- Related: #4071 (validate accepts internally inconsistent bodies — the rule-set extension; complementary, not duplicate: it never mentions the sign path, and its fix would not make `sign_authorisation` call `validate`), #5623 (the artifact-module precedent for sign-side validation), #2290 / #5521 (the RateAuthorisation design/implementation this module serves).
- Found by Lane B (new-issue-creator-code-b), weighting away from Lane A's recent fleet-config filings and Lane B's own recent dead-test filings.

items.body:
## Problem

In `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs`, `RateAuthorisation::validate` is the only validity gate the fold trusts — and it checks exactly two things (issuer match, `rate_den != 0`). Every other validity condition the type's own field docs state is never checked anywhere, `sign_authorisation` never calls `validate` at all, and the fold crowns the highest "valid" version — so a malformed authorisation signs, folds `Live`, and a malformed higher version permanently shadows a good lower one (the fold doc: no older version revives once a higher exists).

- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:152-163` — `validate()` checks only `issuer_id == author` and `rate_den == 0`. Its rustdoc (:146-151) names only those two errors, matching the one field with explicit validity language: `rate_den` is "non-zero in a valid authorisation" (:104-106).
- The unchecked documented conditions: `min_amount` is the "Smallest convertible amount" and `max_amount` the "Largest" (:108-112) — `min > max` is a contradiction no conversion can satisfy; `not_before` is "No conversions before this time" and `expires_at` the "Mandatory expiry: no conversions at or after" (:118-121) — `expires_at <= not_before` is an empty/inverted window; `fee_bps` is a "fee in basis points" (:124-126) — above 10,000 bps the fee exceeds 100% of the conversion; the module doc (:10-14) defines the object as one direction `source_ledger` → `dest_ledger` — identical ledgers are a degenerate self-conversion; `rate_num == 0` makes `apply_rate` return `Some(0)` for every amount (:169-175).
- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:279-311` — `fold_authorisation` filters candidates by `body.validate(author).is_ok()` (:291, under the doc at :262-277: "Among the expected issuer's valid versions the highest is the candidate") and crowns the highest version `Live`. An unchecked-malformed v2 therefore displaces a good v1, and since revocation/supersession never revives a lower version, the authorisation is bricked by its own malformed successor.
- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:313-336` — `sign_authorisation` serializes and signs any body without calling `validate`: even the two existing checks are sign-time unenforced, so an issuer can publish a zero-denominator authorisation the fold will silently drop (`fold` → `None`) while believing it live.

This is Phase 1 library code (#3800, closed), but the Phase 2/3 gateway (#3801/#3802, on #2290) will consume `fold_authorisation`'s `Live` state as its trust input — the gate should mean what the docs say before a gateway builds on it.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-laneB-currencyvalidate/` with `currency.rs` copied verbatim from `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` (production code, md5 `291c105842289c856635a2b69ffd1d72`, identical in the sandbox clone at main `a0ff47b41` and the laptop checkout; only the `#[cfg(test)]` module was stripped and `crate::chain` stubbed to the surface `currency.rs` uses — `validate`/`fold_authorisation`/`apply_rate` are pure and unmodified), `cargo run --release`, using the #2290 worked example from the module's own tests as the baseline body:

- BASELINE (min 1 ≤ max 10,000, window 0 → 4102444800, no fee): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P1 `min_amount=10_001, max_amount=10_000`: `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P2 `not_before=1000, expires_at=1000` (empty window): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P3 `not_before=2000, expires_at=1000` (inverted window): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P4 `fee_bps=Some(20_000)` (a 200% fee): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P5 `rate_num=0`: `validate=Ok(())`, `apply_rate(100)=Some(0)`, fold = `Live`.
- P6 `source_ledger == dest_ledger == "ABC"`: `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- CONTROL `rate_den=0`: `validate=Err(ZeroRateDenominator)`, fold = `None` — the one documented check beyond issuer works.
- P7 shadowing: good v1 + inverted-bounds v2 → fold = `Live` version 2 (min 10001, max 10000); the good v1 is unreachable.

Dedup: title/keyword searches for `RateAuthorisation`, currency-validate, fee_bps and min_amount across open and closed issues find only the #2290 design (open), the closed Phase 1 implementation #3800, and the gateway phases #3801/#3802 — none covers validation completeness.

## Why it matters

`Live` is the fold's promise that an authorisation is usable. Today it also covers authorisations that can never convert (inverted bounds, empty window), that charge more than the converted amount in fees, or that convert a ledger into itself — and because version selection trusts `validate`, one malformed successor silently retires every good earlier version. The issuer-side sign path compounds it: nothing stops publishing a body the fold will drop or crown wrongly. Fixing the gate now is cheap; after the #3801/#3802 gateway treats `Live` as authoritative, each unchecked case becomes a gateway bug instead of a library inconsistency.

## Acceptance criteria

- `RateAuthorisation::validate` rejects, with named `ValidateError` variants: `min_amount > max_amount`; `expires_at <= not_before`; `fee_bps > 10_000`. For `rate_num == 0` and `source_ledger == dest_ledger`, the fix either rejects them in `validate` too or documents explicitly at the field why they are intentionally valid — silence is not an accepted outcome.
- `sign_authorisation` refuses a body that `validate` rejects (sign/validate symmetry), or the asymmetry is documented as intentional at `sign_authorisation` with the reason.
- New unit tests cover each rejected case at both `validate` and the fold (a malformed higher version no longer crowns over a good lower version — it is skipped by the fold's validity filter, like the zero-denominator control), and the existing `currency` tests pass unchanged.
- The `validate` rustdoc lists every condition it checks, so the Phase 2 gateway (#3801/#3802) can rely on the doc as the contract.

# id(issuer-rotation): `fold_rotation_chain` dedups candidates by event id only — duplicate-id entries with a different author/body make the fold input-order dependent, contradicting its determinism contract

## Evidence (verified this run against main `af0847d00a2231c71f6ebb59eba4cc7db197599e`, via `gh api` raw reads; laptop unreachable this run)

`pkgs/id/src/issuer_rotation.rs:497` documents the fold's core contract:

> The fold is deterministic and independent of input order.

The candidate reduction at `pkgs/id/src/issuer_rotation.rs:560-561` does not uphold it:

```rust
candidates.sort_by_key(|(_, event_id, _)| *event_id);
candidates.dedup_by_key(|(_, event_id, _)| *event_id);
```

`sort_by_key` is stable and `dedup_by_key` keeps the *first* of each equal-key run, so when the input slice contains two entries with the **same event id but different rotation bodies**, whichever entry happens to be listed first survives dedup, and the surviving entry alone decides the generation transition (or the fork resolution) afterwards. The filters at lines 543–559 do not save this: they validate each entry on its own merits, and two *distinct, individually valid* bodies can share one event id in the fold's input. Concretely, this changes the folded result under a mere permutation of the same input multiset:

- Same event id, two valid `Routine` bodies by the current generation key naming **different successor keys** (each correctly countersigned by its own successor). Both pass every filter. Listed A-first, generation *g+1*'s key is A's successor; listed B-first, it is B's — instead of the `ChainStatus::Conflicted` the design (§3.2 rule 5) prescribes for two valid transitions claiming the same predecessor.
- Same event id, one valid `Routine` body and one valid `CompromiseRecovery` body (recovery key author). The survivor decides whether the step is a plain advance or a recovery advance with a `RecoveryStep` recorded — purely by input order.

In the production path the event id is the hash of the signed header, so two *decoded events* cannot collide this way today. But `fold_rotation_chain` is a public, documented-as-order-independent pure function over caller-supplied `(author, event_id, rotation)` tuples — its callers supply authors and rotations extracted from events (`fold_rotation_chain` docs, lines 490–496), and any future caller that merges rotation sets from two sources (store + sync feed, journal replay + live) can present the same id twice with divergent extracted fields. The sibling currency fold had exactly this bug class and it was treated as a real defect: #4069 (closed) — "fold_authorisation duplicate highest version folds by input order — no deterministic tie-break". This fold's contract is stronger (it promises order independence outright) and its reduction is weaker (id-only).

## Why it matters

- The fold is the authoritative answer to "which key speaks for generation *g*" for a currency issuer. An order-dependent fold means two replicas folding the same rotation set can disagree on the active issuer key — the exact failure the module exists to prevent (§3.2 rule 5 refuses arrival-order tie-breaks for the same reason).
- The gap is invisible to the current test suite: every fold test passes distinct event ids (`event(1)`, `event(2)`, …), so no test exercises a duplicate id with divergent fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fold_rotation_chain` returns the identical `GenerationChain` for every permutation of the same input multiset, including inputs containing duplicate event ids whose author or rotation body differ. (Deterministic rule for duplicates: e.g. dedup on the full `(event_id, author, rotation)` tuple with a total order over the tuple, or refuse/ignore all-but-one by a content-derived order — any rule that is a function of the multiset, not of the listing order.)
- A property test (per the repo testing doctrine: the oracle is permutation invariance of the fold) shuffles inputs — including duplicate-id/divergent-field entries — and asserts identical output; it fails on the current code and passes after the fix.
- Existing `issuer_rotation` tests still pass (`cargo test -p id --lib issuer_rotation` on the laptop or CI per house rules).
- Dedup behaviour for the ordinary duplicate case (identical tuples listed twice) is unchanged: the transition still counts once.

items.body:
## Summary
`RateAuthorisation::validate` in the new `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` (PR #3888, main `c3fda1c4`) checks exactly two things — issuer == event author and `rate_den != 0` (currency.rs:170-180). Every other internally inconsistent body folds as `Live`: the fold's only validity gate is this function (currency.rs:313-320), so a signed authorisation that can never legitimately convert — or that misprices every conversion — is indistinguishable from a good one for every consumer of the fold.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe)
Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-currency/` on the laptop — verbatim `validate` from currency.rs (reference copy sha256 `8f68982526219dff920586495a076d2c1a33f87fe3b6716a74e561ea821b9493` @ `c3fda1c4`). All of these return `Ok(())`:

```
validate(min>max) -> Ok(())                                   min_amount 10000, max_amount 1
validate(expires_at==not_before (empty window)) -> Ok(())     2000 / 2000
validate(expires_at<not_before) -> Ok(())                     2000 / 3000
validate(fee_bps 99999 (>100%)) -> Ok(())                     fee is 999.99%
validate(empty ledgers) -> Ok(())                             source_ledger "" and dest_ledger ""
validate(source==dest ledger) -> Ok(())                       ABC -> ABC
validate(rate_num 0 (zero rate)) -> Ok(())                    every conversion yields 0
validate(total_cap 0) -> Ok(())                               cap permits nothing
validate(empty allowlist (allows nobody)) -> Ok(())           AuthorisedCallers::Allowlist([])
test validate_accepts_internally_inconsistent_bodies ... ok
```

(Sanity: the two documented checks do fire — `rate_den = 0` returns `ZeroRateDenominator`.)

## Why it matters
`validate` is the library-level contract the fold, and later the Phase 2 gateway checks (#3801: window, min/max, remaining volume at submission), rely on. A body with `min_amount > max_amount`, an empty/inverted validity window, or `fee_bps > 10000` can never be caught downstream as "invalid" — the gateway's live-state checks would evaluate a nonsense window and nonsense bounds as if they were policy, and different consumers can disagree about shapes like a zero rate or a same-ledger "conversion". The field docs in this same file state the invariants in prose ("Rate denominator; non-zero in a valid authorisation", "Mandatory expiry", "Optional fee in basis points") — `rate_den` is the only one enforced.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `validate` rejects, with named `ValidateError` variants: `min_amount > max_amount`; `expires_at <= not_before`; `fee_bps > Some(10000)`; empty `source_ledger` or `dest_ledger`; `source_ledger == dest_ledger`.
- [ ] Shapes that are arguably legitimate-but-dead (zero `rate_num`, zero `total_cap`, empty allowlist) are either rejected with named variants or explicitly documented as valid in the field docs — one stated rule, tested either way.
- [ ] Tests cover each rejected shape; existing currency tests still pass; the fold ignores the newly invalid bodies (covered by the existing fold-filter test pattern).

Distinct from: #3801 (gateway submission-time checks against accounts/tiers — it assumes a valid folded object), #4069 (duplicate-version fold tie-break, same file, different defect), #4063 (app_manifest parser validation, different module).

Phase 2 of the RateAuthorisation set tracked by issue #2290 — for the issue #2062 gateway follow-ons to build on. Design record: the task 5741 triage comment on issue #2290 (verification flow steps 1–4). Depends on the Phase 1 schema/fold issue in this set.

Build in the control plane / gateway:
- Verification flow: (1) chain decode + signature, header verifying key == body issuer_id; (2) LP-tier eligibility from the control-plane registry (issue #2063 §3 tiers); (3) account-control chain — the conversion's source/dest liquidity accounts must be exactly the account-factory binding records for the issuer, neither closing/closed; (4) live-state checks at submission: highest version folded, not revoked, window, caller authorisation, min/max, remaining_volume.
- Revocation-set materialisation: fold `currency.rate_authorisation_revoke` events into the set the gateway consults at submission time. Revocation stops new conversions only; posted conversions are untouched (issue #2063 §4.4).
- Every failure is pre-flight (FAILED_PRE_SUBMIT) with no TigerBeetle writes.

Acceptance: tests cover each step failing closed (bad signature, wrong issuer, unbound account, revoked, expired, cap-exhausted, unauthorised caller) with zero ledger writes.

items.body:
From the conversion-engine design on #2063 §2 (feeds #2043; parent epic #2056; relates to the issuance-in-graph investigation #2041).

Define the **RateAuthorisation as a signed ID-graph object**:

- Schema for the fields in #2063 §2: id, version, issuer (LP) identity, source/dest ledgers, integer-rational rate (rate_num/rate_den, scale-aware), per-conversion min/max, total cap, authorised callers (any / allowlist / single counterparty), not_before + mandatory expires_at, one-direction-only (reverse is a separate object).
- Signing: the object is signed with the issuer's ID key; specify how the gateway (#2062) verifies the signature chains to the identity controlling both liquidity accounts.
- Revocation: representation + how the control plane's revocation set is checked at submission; revocation stops new conversions and never touches posted ones.
- Quote binding: how a short-lived single-conversion quote references an authorisation (authorisation_id + amounts + fee + expiry).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] A schema + worked example (ABC→123 at 0.8123, both directions as separate objects) recorded in a design doc or on this issue.
- [ ] Signature-verification and revocation-check flows specified precisely enough for the #2062 gateway to implement against.
- [ ] Anything buildable that falls out is filed as follow-ups linked here.

Schema/design work only in this issue; the gateway implementation belongs to #2062's follow-ons.

items.body:
# Phase 4 of #6487 — closing sign-surface inventory: disposition every public signing entry point in pkgs/id against the sign-time refusal contract

Design: #6487 (sign only what receipt would accept — one sign-time
refusal contract for `pkgs/id`). Design doc:
`files/designs/code-id-sign-time-refusal.md` in the
keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

**Gated on Phases 1–3 of #6487** (Phase 1: #6422 + #6443;
Phase 2: #6424 + #6434; Phase 3: #6447 + #6451 + #6469). Do not
start the inventory until they have landed; keep this issue
`status/blocked` until then.

## Scope

Produce a closing inventory of **every public signing entry point
in `pkgs/id`** (every `pub fn sign_*`, `Signed*::sign`, and any
public method whose purpose is producing a signed object),
dispositioned against the #6487 contract with file:line evidence:

- **enforced** — the signer mirrors every unconditional receipt
  rule decidable from its own inputs; name the phase that did it;
- **deliberately receipt-only** — every unchecked receipt rule is
  class (d) receiver-state; name the rule and the reason it is
  not decidable at the seam;
- **gap** — a decidable unconditional receipt rule is still
  signable-around: file it as a follow-up issue from the audit
  (do not fix it inside this phase).

Required dispositions (named in the design doc):

- `sign_revoke` (currency.rs) — no `RateAuthorisationRevoke`
  validator exists and the fold applies no validity filter to
  revokes: state whether a revoke rule set is worth filing
  (neighbouring #4071's rule-set extension), or record "no
  receipt rule exists — nothing to mirror" with the evidence.
- `directory::sign_up` / `sign_up_keyed` — stateful admission
  methods, not pure signers: expected disposition is out of the
  contract's scope, with the reason stated, not assumed.
- The documents/chain builder symmetry (#3231's estate) —
  confirm the builders still apply their receipt rules, or
  disposition the difference.
- `SignedArtifact::sign_unchecked` — the deliberate
  crate-private bypass: disposition conforming under rule 4 of
  #6487 (crate-private, `*_unchecked` naming), or file the gap.
- Replication receiver test bypass helpers (the
  `sign_unbounded` pattern) — same rule-4 disposition.
- Any signing entry point the Phases 1–3 work surfaced that
  this list does not name — the inventory, not this list, is
  the proof of completeness.

Also land the contract statement in the crate's documentation:
the rule ("sign only what receipt would accept") and the four
decidability classes (intrinsic / signer-relative /
seam-extended / receiver-state), where a future `sign_*`
author will find it before adding a new signer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An inventory table covering every public signing entry
      point in `pkgs/id`, each dispositioned as above with
      file:line evidence, posted on this issue (and in the
      crate docs if that is where the contract statement lands).
- [ ] The four required dispositions above are each answered
      explicitly — none silently skipped.
- [ ] Any gap found is filed as its own follow-up issue and
      linked here; nothing is fixed inside this phase beyond
      the docs statement.
- [ ] The contract statement (rule + decidability classes) is
      present in the crate's documentation.
- [ ] Receipt behaviour is unchanged by this phase (docs and
      inventory only).

🤖 Filed by the repo design architect (fleet) as Phase 4 of
#6487, gated on Phases 1–3.
